q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

problems: percentages that do not follow from the figures written beside them (recompute from those figures): 7.3%

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
No — the data disagree with that premise: order‑date net ROAS fell, while net profit worsened (loss grew).

Evidence (2026-10-07 → 2026-10-13 vs 2026-09-30 → 2026-10-06)
- Net profit: measured −₹35,790 → −₹61,080; change −₹25,290 (−70.7%). — Measured  
- Contribution margin (order‑P&L): measured ₹333,755 → ₹314,280; change −₹19,475. — Measured  
- Ad spend (P&L basis): measured ₹369,545 → ₹375,359; change +₹5,814 (+1.6%). — Measured  
- Net sales (order date): measured ₹641,932 → ₹525,092; change −₹116,840 (−18.2%). — Measured  
- Net ROAS (derived = contribution margin ÷ ad spend, order date): derived ~0.9x → ~0.8x; change −7.3%. — Derived

Plain interpretation (measured, not assumed)
- The larger loss is explained by a fall in contribution margin (~−₹19.5k) plus a small rise in ad spend (~+₹5.8k); together these account for the net profit worsening. — Measured
- Because contribution margin fell more than ad spend, net ROAS (contribution per ₹1 ad spend) also fell — so ROAS is not increasing on the order‑date/net basis. — Measured/Derived

What remains unverified (possible reasons the business or platform UI might have shown an increase)
- Platform‑reported or gross ROAS (gross sales ÷ platform spend) was not fetched and can differ from order‑date net ROAS.  
- Product‑ or campaign‑level allocated ROAS (product net ROAS (allocated) / product gross ROAS (allocated)) may have behaved differently; net_roas catalogue metric was broken so I derived ROAS from contribution margin and ad spend.  
- Segment-level drivers (which ad_platforms, campaigns or SKUs caused the margin drop) — totals are shown above but I did not break them down here.
